purpose: Design document defining how start-design, start-plan and start-requirements are structured as orchestrators with a shared context-gathering framework and per-skill collection rules.
summary: Overview of the orchestrator pattern shared by the three create skills
Orchestrator structure and responsibility split between main context, document search, code-collection agent, review and post-processing
Rationale for running document authoring in the main context because of user dialogue
Common context-gathering framework: document search via query-db skills called directly, code exploration via a general-purpose agent
Collection result handoff via return values with no session directory, and inline prompt template for the code agent
Failure handling: stop and report on search failure, skipped search or agent error; zero results is valid
Per-skill design for start-design inputs, start-plan phases and collection matrix, start-requirements agent matrix
Existing components used and the reason for not using sessions
tasks: Designing or modifying the start-design, start-plan or start-requirements orchestrators
Changing context gathering behavior or search skill invocation

Reviewing create-skill design documents for consistency
Writing or editing SKILL.md for create-style skills
